summary.oneLiner: A quarter where the bank beat essentially every one of its own FY27 guidance parameters simultaneously — advances +17.97% against 10–12% guided, GNPA at 1.57% against a 1.50% March-27 target already nearly met, credit cost 0.49% against 0.75%, ROE 18.07% against 16.50%, slippage 0.60% against 0.80% — with NII crossing INR10,000cr for the first time. But net profit grew only 2.19%, because a INR1,000cr treasury shortfall and INR1,500cr of higher provisions absorbed the operating gains. The new MD, Brajesh Kumar Singh, has explicitly reordered priorities: **"first thing is efficiency, then only growth,"** with the sub-30% CASA ratio named as his top personal fix and NIM at 2.52% the structural weak spot.

guidance (critical — verify next quarter:
FY27 targets, restated on this call against Q1 achievement:
- **NIM 2.50–2.60%** — at 2.52%; "we will try to better it… we have all the ability to raise it further, even more than 2.60%. But guidance remains at 2.60%."
- **CASA 30–32% by March 2027** — at 29.70%.
- **GNPA 1.50% / NNPA 0.40% by March 2027** — at 1.57% / 0.36% (NNPA already surpassed).
- **PCR 93.50%** — at 94.76%.
- **Slippage ratio 0.80%** — at 0.60%.
- **Credit cost 0.75%** — at 0.51%.
- **ROE 16.50% / ROA 1.01–1.05% / EPS INR20** — at 18.07% / 1.04% / INR21.47. On ROA: "ROA in excess of 1% is okay… Even if we are protecting at 1.01%–1.02%, will be happy."
- **Deposit growth 9–10%**, now aspiring to **11–12%**; business growth 10–11%; advances 10–12% — all already exceeded.
- **FY27 net profit ~INR19,000 cr** — "when we analyze, we will be again making, everything goes correct, around 19,000 crores of profit."
- **Foreign-currency funding: USD 2.3–2.5 billion** across FCNR-B, ECB and OFCB. July target was USD 750mn; **USD 775mn already raised**, with an endeavour to **cross USD 1 billion within July**. Cost ~6.50% plus CRR/SLR dispensation worth another 20–25bps, landing below the current ~6.58% bulk deposit cost.
- **ECL transition:** ~**INR10,000cr** of extra provisioning identified across stages, plus perhaps INR2,000cr of mark-to-market on the investment book, i.e. **INR12,000–13,000cr total**. Capital dent of **1.2–1.25%** if absorbed in one year. **Plan is to absorb over 2 years against the 5 years RBI allows**, with **no capital raise required**. **Technology dry run by October 2026.** Run-rate credit cost impact estimated at only **4–5bps** ("not even 10 basis points").
- **ECLGS 5.0 / Emergency Line of Credit:** ~INR90,000cr of accounts screened, ~INR18,000cr assessed as eligible, **INR11,000cr+ sanctioned and INR10,000cr+ already disbursed**, with a further **INR5,000–6,000cr expected**.
- **250 new branches this year** (34 already opened) on a base of 10,131.
- **Digital spend of over INR3,000 cr earmarked this year**, a substantial portion toward AI.
order book & pipeline: The corporate credit pipeline was disclosed with unusual specificity: **~INR50,000cr across ~92–100 accounts** — 45 accounts sanctioned but undisbursed worth ~INR18,000cr, plus 47 accounts of "good proposals, which are sanctionable and disbursable" worth ~INR32,000cr. On top of this sits the residual ECLGS 5.0 runway of INR5,000–6,000cr. Corporate pricing is described as improving — "we are getting little 10 paisa, 20 paisa here and there. If we are bargaining, we are getting" — and 86% of the corporate book is now A-rated or above, up from last quarter.
segment / subsidiary detail:
- **RAM (59% of advances, +21.20%)** — the strategic priority, up 1pp of mix YoY. The rationale given was explicit: better leverage, diversified risk, lower credit cost, and priority-sector reckoning. Blended RAM yield runs **~50bps above corporate**, offset by higher operating cost. Retail led at +35.88%, vehicle +26.34%, housing +17.85%, MSME +15.12%.
- **Gold loans (INR2.59 lakh cr)** — claimed market leadership. Described as structurally attractive: near-cash collateral, negligible credit cost, no capital provision, LTV 60–65%. Stable in the south and expanding elsewhere. This is the quiet compounding asset in the book.
- **Corporate** — deliberately being repriced. Sub-7% legacy loans are reset in the bank's favour at renewal, and "sometime we do not mind taking prepayment also." Growth is skewed to better-rated names.
- **Treasury / PSLC** — the two swing factors this quarter, moving in opposite directions and largely cancelling each other's effect on profit.
- **Subsidiaries** — ~5 subsidiaries and ~5 associates contributing ~INR320cr of profit to the parent. **Canara HSBC Life and Canara Robeco listed last year** and are both performing; the MD described a threefold benefit — agency/distribution commission across 10,131 branches, rising subsidiary valuation, and appreciation on the bank's own shareholding. Governance kept at arm's length via independent boards.
- **Agriculture** — the monsoon-exposure question was answered structurally: weak-rainfall districts get declared distressed by the SLBC and District Level Technical Committee, triggering dispensations; Fasal Bima provides further cover; rain-fed area is shrinking; and the KCC portfolio is "not very huge." Segmental slippages nonetheless show agriculture (INR727cr) and MSME (INR697cr) as the main sources, against retail INR326cr and gold INR20–30cr, on a total of INR1,781cr.
growth verticals / optionality:
- **Liability repricing is the central value lever.** The plan is to replace high-cost bulk deposits (~6.58%) with a combination of retail term deposits, individual savings and foreign-currency funding at an effective sub-6.30% after CRR/SLR dispensation. Individual savings grew 12.48% and retail term deposits 9.10% — described as heartening in a tight market. Month-on-month, bulk outflow versus inflow is running **29–30bps in the bank's favour**.
- **CD ratio expansion from 75% to 80%** shifts assets from investments (yield 6.90%) into advances (yield 8.00%) — a **110bps** pickup on every rupee moved, and the mechanical driver behind NII crossing INR10,000cr.
- **Digital and AI** — over INR3,000cr earmarked, with the MD wanting AI done "in a very consolidated way, not in piecemeal way." He argued a structural advantage from being headquartered in Bengaluru with tech-savvy staff. He was candid that the constraint is adoption, not availability: "Digital journeys are there but adoption level for all the journeys are not that high."
- **Branch expansion** — 250 new branches this year, plus subsidiary-driven account acquisition synergy (a customer buying a group mutual fund needs a savings account).
6a. moat & competitive position:
- **Distribution scale.** 10,131 branches, expanding by 250 this year, monetised three ways through the listed subsidiaries (commission, valuation, shareholding).
- **Gold loan leadership** at INR2.59 lakh cr — capital-light, credit-cost-light, collateral-backed, and structurally embedded in southern banking behaviour ("people collateralize gold for all their banking needs").
- **Provision and capital buffers.** PCR at 94.76% and CRAR at 17.17% against an 11.50% requirement mean the entire ECL transition can be absorbed in two years with no capital raise — a genuine competitive advantage versus thinner-capitalised peers facing the same regulatory change.
- **Asset quality position.** Total SMA under 3% of the book, described as "some of the industry best number," with 86% of the corporate book A-rated or above.
margins & cost dynamics:
NIM at 2.52% is the acknowledged structural weakness, and the MD did not defend it — he arrived from a bank running 3.32%–3.50% and named the cause precisely: CASA below 30% forcing bulk-deposit dependence. The repair plan attacks both sides. On liabilities: grow individual savings and retail term deposits, replace bulk with FCNR-B/ECB/OFCB at an effective sub-6.30%, and capture the 29–30bps monthly favourable gap on bulk roll-over. On assets: reprice legacy sub-7% corporate loans at reset (accepting prepayment where necessary), shift mix toward RAM (~50bps yield premium), and raise the CD ratio to move funds from 6.90% investments into 8.00% advances.

Yields have "largely stabilised" now that the 100bps FY26 repo cut has fully transmitted through a 53% repo-linked book. The MD was clear that neither side alone suffices — "one side will not help… we have to get traction from both side little here and little there."
capex / expansion (watch slippage):
- **250 new branches in FY27**, 34 opened.
- **Digital spend of over INR3,000cr**, ~8% of total IT cost allocation, with a substantial share toward AI.
- **ECL technology readiness** — knowledge partner engaged; PD, LGD and EAD modalities in place; **dry run scheduled for October 2026**.
- **Foreign-currency funding programme** — USD 2.3–2.5bn target, USD 775mn raised in July with USD 1bn targeted within the month.
capital allocation: The ECL transition dominates. Against an identified INR12,000–13,000cr requirement, the bank has PCR at 94.76%, CRAR at 17.17% (CET1 12.91%) versus an 11.50% requirement, and expected FY27 profit of ~INR19,000cr. Management will voluntarily absorb the hit over **two years rather than the five RBI permits**, taking a 1.2–1.25% capital dent, and confirmed **no capital raise is needed**. There are no hidden or floating provisions beyond standard-asset provisioning — the MD said so directly when asked. Growth is being funded from internal accrual and low-cost deposit substitution rather than capital issuance.
risks & watch-items:
- **SMA-2 more than doubled to INR3,482cr from INR1,394cr, and SMA-0 rose to INR3,315cr from INR862cr.** The explanation — three or four large government-guaranteed consortium accounts oscillating between SMA buckets, with one already back to SMA-0 and another out entirely — is specific and plausible, and SMA-1 fell in the same period. But it relies on management's word about unnamed accounts, and total SMA is under 3%. Watch whether the oscillation stops.
- **Net profit grew only 2.19% despite operating outperformance.** The treasury tailwind of FY26 has become a ~INR1,000cr headwind and will not return while yields stay hard.
- **PSLC income is Q1-loaded and non-repeatable within the year** — INR1,947cr this quarter against INR393cr in Q4, with only INR200–300cr expected in Q2 and effectively nothing in H2. This is the single biggest reason not to annualise Q1 profitability.
- **NIM at 2.52%** remains among the weakest in the peer set, and the fix is multi-year.
- **ECL uncertainty on mark-to-market.** Management was honest that the investment-book M2M component is unknowable — "we do not have exact idea about M2M… nobody has got that idea."
- **Agriculture and MSME account for the bulk of slippages** (INR1,424cr of INR1,781cr), and monsoon risk sits in the KCC book, albeit with regulatory dispensations available.
- **Fee income sluggish** at +5.35% YoY and down ~INR200cr sequentially — explained as seasonal booking of government commissions and service charges in Q4.
- **New MD transition.** Brajesh Kumar Singh is reorienting the bank toward efficiency over growth; the strategic direction is credible but unproven at this bank's scale.
management quality / tone:
Brajesh Kumar Singh opened by walking through every FY27 guidance parameter against Q1 achievement, line by line — an unusually accountable format, and legitimate given that the bank beat all of them. He was direct about weaknesses rather than defensive: NIM "is towards the lowest side," CASA below peers "to the likes of Central Bank of India, Bank of Maharashtra," and digital adoption "not that high" despite journeys being built. Asked what he wants to change, he gave three specific answers — CASA, HR ("I would like them to not only talk about deposit and advances, rather they should talk about ROE, NIM"), and ethics. He disclosed granular numbers on demand: segmental slippages, interest on IT refund, cost of bulk deposits, credit pipeline account counts, gold loan LTV, ECL quantum. He also declined to overstate — on ECL M2M he simply said nobody knows, and on the RAM-versus-corporate yield differential he offered to send the exact number rather than guess.

The one soft spot is the SMA explanation: credible and internally consistent, but resting on unnamed accounts. The repeated defensive framing — "our performance should be seen in perspective of the total ecosystem, how our peers have fared" — is understandable in a quarter when profit grew 2%, but it recurs often enough to note.
non-obvious takeaways:
- The headline profit growth of 2.19% badly understates the quarter. Operating performance beat every guidance parameter; the profit line was absorbed by a ~INR1,000cr treasury reversal and ~INR1,500cr of higher provisions (including ~INR300cr of staff incentive). Conversely, Q1 profitability cannot be annualised because PSLC income of INR1,947cr is a first-quarter phenomenon that all but disappears in H2.
- Canara is arbitraging the same funding squeeze that is cutting Bandhan's ROA guidance. While Bandhan raised INR30cr of FCNR-B and lost 30bps of planned NIM, Canara is targeting USD 2.3–2.5bn at an effective sub-6.30% to displace 6.58% bulk deposits. Scale and franchise reach are converting a sector-wide headwind into a spread opportunity.
- The CD ratio move from 75% to 80% is the mechanical driver behind NII crossing INR10,000cr: every rupee shifted from investments (6.90%) to advances (8.00%) picks up 110bps, independent of any pricing action.
- Choosing to absorb ECL in two years rather than the permitted five, without a capital raise, is a confidence signal — and it front-loads the pain into a period when profits are ~INR19,000cr a year, leaving the outer years clean.
- The ECL run-rate impact of 4–5bps on credit cost is far smaller than the one-time INR12,000–13,000cr transition would suggest, because the bank's PCR is already at 94.76% and NPAs are fully provided. The gap sits almost entirely in SMA-1 and SMA-2.
- Gold loans at INR2.59 lakh cr — roughly 20% of advances — carry near-zero credit cost, no capital provision and 60–65% LTV. This is a materially better-quality growth engine than the headline RAM number alone conveys.
- The new MD's ranking of priorities ("first thing is efficiency, then only growth") is the opposite of how a PSU bank beating every growth target would usually position itself, and is the most important forward signal on the call.

- **ECLGS 5.0 / Emergency Line of Credit:** ~INR90,000cr of accounts screened, ~INR18,000cr assessed as eligible, **INR11,000cr+ sanctioned and INR10,000cr+ already disbursed**, with a further **INR5,000–6,000cr expected**.
- **250 new branches this year** (34 already opened) on a base of 10,131.
- **Digital spend of over INR3,000 cr earmarked this year**, a substantial portion toward AI.

On top of this sits the residual ECLGS 5.0 runway of INR5,000–6,000cr. Corporate pricing is described as improving — "we are getting little 10 paisa, 20 paisa here and there. If we are bargaining, we are getting" — and 86% of the corporate book is now A-rated or above, up from last quarter.
segment / subsidiary detail:
- **RAM (59% of advances, +21.20%)** — the strategic priority, up 1pp of mix YoY. The rationale given was explicit: better leverage, diversified risk, lower credit cost, and priority-sector reckoning. Blended RAM yield runs **~50bps above corporate**, offset by higher operating cost. Retail led at +35.88%, vehicle +26.34%, housing +17.85%, MSME +15.12%.
- **Gold loans (INR2.59 lakh cr)** — claimed market leadership. Described as structurally attractive: near-cash collateral, negligible credit cost, no capital provision, LTV 60–65%. Stable in the south and expanding elsewhere. This is the quiet compounding asset in the book.
- **Corporate** — deliberately being repriced. Sub-7% legacy loans are reset in the bank's favour at renewal, and "sometime we do not mind taking prepayment also." Growth is skewed to better-rated names.
- **Treasury / PSLC** — the two swing factors this quarter, moving in opposite directions and largely cancelling each other's effect on profit.
- **Subsidiaries** — ~5 subsidiaries and ~5 associates contributing ~INR320cr of profit to the parent. **Canara HSBC Life and Canara Robeco listed last year** and are both performing; the MD described a threefold benefit — agency/distribution commission across 10,131 branches, rising subsidiary valuation, and appreciation on the bank's own shareholding. - **Digital and AI** — over INR3,000cr earmarked, with the MD wanting AI done "in a very consolidated way, not in piecemeal way." 6a. moat & competitive position:
- **Distribution scale.** 10,131 branches, expanding by 250 this year, monetised three ways through the listed subsidiaries (commission, valuation, shareholding).
- **Gold loan leadership** at INR2.59 lakh cr — capital-light, credit-cost-light, collateral-backed, and structurally embedded in southern banking behaviour ("people collateralize gold for all their banking needs").
- **Provision and capital buffers.** PCR at 94.76% and CRAR at 17.17% against an 11.50% requirement mean the entire ECL transition can be absorbed in two years with no capital raise — a genuine competitive advantage versus thinner-capitalised peers facing the same regulatory change.

margins & cost dynamics:
NIM at 2.52% is the acknowledged structural weakness, and the MD did not defend it — he arrived from a bank running 3.32%–3.50% and named the cause precisely: CASA below 30% forcing bulk-deposit dependence. On assets: reprice legacy sub-7% corporate loans at reset (accepting prepayment where necessary), shift mix toward RAM (~50bps yield premium), and raise the CD ratio to move funds from 6.90% investments into 8.00% advances.

Yields have "largely stabilised" now that the 100bps FY26 repo cut has fully transmitted through a 53% repo-linked book. The MD was clear that neither side alone suffices — "one side will not help… we have to get traction from both side little here and little there."
capex / expansion (watch slippage):
- **250 new branches in FY27**, 34 opened.
- **Digital spend of over INR3,000cr**, ~8% of total IT cost allocation, with a substantial share toward AI.
- **ECL technology readiness** — knowledge partner engaged; PD, LGD and EAD modalities in place; **dry run scheduled for October 2026**.
- **Foreign-currency funding programme** — USD 2.3–2.5bn target, USD 775mn raised in July with USD 1bn targeted within the month.
capital allocation: The ECL transition dominates. Against an identified INR12,000–13,000cr requirement, the bank has PCR at 94.76%, CRAR at 17.17% (CET1 12.91%) versus an 11.50% requirement, and expected FY27 profit of ~INR19,000cr. risks & watch-items:
- **SMA-2 more than doubled to INR3,482cr from INR1,394cr, and SMA-0 rose to INR3,315cr from INR862cr.** The explanation — three or four large government-guaranteed consortium accounts oscillating between SMA buckets, with one already back to SMA-0 and another out entirely — is specific and plausible, and SMA-1 fell in the same period. But it relies on management's word about unnamed accounts, and total SMA is under 3%. Watch whether the oscillation stops.
- **Net profit grew only 2.19% despite operating outperformance.** The treasury tailwind of FY26 has become a ~INR1,000cr headwind and will not return while yields stay hard.
- **PSLC income is Q1-loaded and non-repeatable within the year** — INR1,947cr this quarter against INR393cr in Q4, with only INR200–300cr expected in Q2 and effectively nothing in H2. This is the single biggest reason not to annualise Q1 profitability.
- **NIM at 2.52%** remains among the weakest in the peer set, and the fix is multi-year.
- **ECL uncertainty on mark-to-market.** Management was honest that the investment-book M2M component is unknowable — "we do not have exact idea about M2M… nobody has got that idea."
- **Agriculture and MSME account for the bulk of slippages** (INR1,424cr of INR1,781cr), and monsoon risk sits in the KCC book, albeit with regulatory dispensations available.
- **Fee income sluggish** at +5.35% YoY and down ~INR200cr sequentially — explained as seasonal booking of government commissions and service charges in Q4.
- **New MD transition.** Brajesh Kumar Singh is reorienting the bank toward efficiency over growth; the strategic direction is credible but unproven at this bank's scale.
management quality / tone:
Brajesh Kumar Singh opened by walking through every FY27 guidance parameter against Q1 achievement, line by line — an unusually accountable format, and legitimate given that the bank beat all of them. He was direct about weaknesses rather than defensive: NIM "is towards the lowest side," CASA below peers "to the likes of Central Bank of India, Bank of Maharashtra," and digital adoption "not that high" despite journeys being built. Asked what he wants to change, he gave three specific answers — CASA, HR ("I would like them to not only talk about deposit and advances, rather they should talk about ROE, NIM"), and ethics. He disclosed granular numbers on demand: segmental slippages, interest on IT refund, cost of bulk deposits, credit pipeline account counts, gold loan LTV, ECL quantum. He also declined to overstate — on ECL M2M he simply said nobody knows, and on the RAM-versus-corporate yield differential he offered to send the exact number rather than guess.

The one soft spot is the SMA explanation: credible and internally consistent, but resting on unnamed accounts. The repeated defensive framing — "our performance should be seen in perspective of the total ecosystem, how our peers have fared" — is understandable in a quarter when profit grew 2%, but it recurs often enough to note.
non-obvious takeaways:
- The headline profit growth of 2.19% badly understates the quarter. Operating performance beat every guidance parameter; the profit line was absorbed by a ~INR1,000cr treasury reversal and ~INR1,500cr of higher provisions (including ~INR300cr of staff incentive). Conversely, Q1 profitability cannot be annualised because PSLC income of INR1,947cr is a first-quarter phenomenon that all but disappears in H2.
- Canara is arbitraging the same funding squeeze that is cutting Bandhan's ROA guidance. While Bandhan raised INR30cr of FCNR-B and lost 30bps of planned NIM, Canara is targeting USD 2.3–2.5bn at an effective sub-6.30% to displace 6.58% bulk deposits. Scale and franchise reach are converting a sector-wide headwind into a spread opportunity.
- The CD ratio move from 75% to 80% is the mechanical driver behind NII crossing INR10,000cr: every rupee shifted from investments (6.90%) to advances (8.00%) picks up 110bps, independent of any pricing action.
- Choosing to absorb ECL in two years rather than the permitted five, without a capital raise, is a confidence signal — and it front-loads the pain into a period when profits are ~INR19,000cr a year, leaving the outer years clean.
- The ECL run-rate impact of 4–5bps on credit cost is far smaller than the one-time INR12,000–13,000cr transition would suggest, because the bank's PCR is already at 94.76% and NPAs are fully provided. The gap sits almost entirely in SMA-1 and SMA-2.
- Gold loans at INR2.59 lakh cr — roughly 20% of advances — carry near-zero credit cost, no capital provision and 60–65% LTV. This is a materially better-quality growth engine than the headline RAM number alone conveys.
- The new MD's ranking of priorities ("first thing is efficiency, then only growth") is the opposite of how a PSU bank beating every growth target would usually position itself, and is the most important forward signal on the call.

hero.oneLiner: A quarter where the bank beat essentially every one of its own FY27 guidance parameters simultaneously — advances +17.97% against 10–12% guided, GNPA at 1.57% against a 1.50% March-27 target already nearly met, credit cost 0.49% against 0.75%, ROE 18.07% against 16.50%, slippage 0.60% against 0.80% — with NII crossing INR10,000cr for the first time. But net profit grew only 2.19%, because a INR1,000cr treasury shortfall and INR1,500cr of higher provisions absorbed the operating gains. The new MD, Brajesh Kumar Singh, has explicitly reordered priorities: **"first thing is efficiency, then only growth,"** with the sub-30% CASA ratio named as his top personal fix and NIM at 2.52% the structural weak spot.

- **PSLC income is Q1-loaded and non-repeatable within the year** — INR1,947cr this quarter against INR393cr in Q4, with only INR200–300cr expected in Q2 and effectively nothing in H2. This is the single biggest reason not to annualise Q1 profitability.
- **NIM at 2.52%** remains among the weakest in the peer set, and the fix is multi-year.
- **ECL uncertainty on mark-to-market.** Management was honest that the investment-book M2M component is unknowable — "we do not have exact idea about M2M… nobody has got that idea."
- **Agriculture and MSME account for the bulk of slippages** (INR1,424cr of INR1,781cr), and monsoon risk sits in the KCC book, albeit with regulatory dispensations available.
- **Fee income sluggish** at +5.35% YoY and down ~INR200cr sequentially — explained as seasonal booking of government commissions and service charges in Q4.
- **New MD transition.** Brajesh Kumar Singh is reorienting the bank toward efficiency over growth; the strategic direction is credible but unproven at this bank's scale.

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body:
- The headline profit growth of 2.19% badly understates the quarter. Operating performance beat every guidance parameter; the profit line was absorbed by a ~INR1,000cr treasury reversal and ~INR1,500cr of higher provisions (including ~INR300cr of staff incentive). Conversely, Q1 profitability cannot be annualised because PSLC income of INR1,947cr is a first-quarter phenomenon that all but disappears in H2.
- Canara is arbitraging the same funding squeeze that is cutting Bandhan's ROA guidance. While Bandhan raised INR30cr of FCNR-B and lost 30bps of planned NIM, Canara is targeting USD 2.3–2.5bn at an effective sub-6.30% to displace 6.58% bulk deposits. Scale and franchise reach are converting a sector-wide headwind into a spread opportunity.
- The CD ratio move from 75% to 80% is the mechanical driver behind NII crossing INR10,000cr: every rupee shifted from investments (6.90%) to advances (8.00%) picks up 110bps, independent of any pricing action.
- Choosing to absorb ECL in two years rather than the permitted five, without a capital raise, is a confidence signal — and it front-loads the pain into a period when profits are ~INR19,000cr a year, leaving the outer years clean.
- The ECL run-rate impact of 4–5bps on credit cost is far smaller than the one-time INR12,000–13,000cr transition would suggest, because the bank's PCR is already at 94.76% and NPAs are fully provided. The gap sits almost entirely in SMA-1 and SMA-2.
- Gold loans at INR2.59 lakh cr — roughly 20% of advances — carry near-zero credit cost, no capital provision and 60–65% LTV. This is a materially better-quality growth engine than the headline RAM number alone conveys.
- The new MD's ranking of priorities ("first thing is efficiency, then only growth") is the opposite of how a PSU bank beating every growth target would usually position itself, and is the most important forward signal on the call.

qoq_log.title: QoQ change log (fill each quarter)
qoq_log.body:
- **Q1 FY27 (this):** Global business INR29.05 lakh cr (+14.37%); advances INR12.93 lakh cr (**+17.97%** vs 10–12% guided); deposits INR16.12 lakh cr (+11.63%). **NII crossed INR10,000cr for the first time at INR10,215cr (+13.39%)**, helped by CD ratio moving 75% → 80%. Net profit INR4,856cr (**+2.19% only**) — operating beat absorbed by treasury falling to INR654cr from INR1,617cr and provisions rising to INR3,780cr from INR2,252cr. **Every FY27 guidance parameter beaten:** GNPA 1.57% (target 1.50% by Mar-27), NNPA 0.36% (0.40%), PCR 94.76% (93.50%), credit cost 0.51% (0.75%), slippage 0.60% (0.80%), ROE 18.07% (16.50%), ROA 1.04% (1.01–1.05%), EPS INR21.47 (INR20). NIM 2.52% within the 2.50–2.60% band. CASA 29.70% vs a 30–32% March-27 target. RAM 59% of advances (+21.20%); gold book INR2.59 lakh cr. **PSLC income INR1,947cr — a Q1-loaded item that will not repeat in H2.** SMA-2 rose to INR3,482cr and SMA-0 to INR3,315cr on 3–4 government-guaranteed consortium accounts. **ECL: INR12,000–13,000cr identified, to be absorbed over 2 years (vs 5 allowed) with no capital raise; dry run in October 2026; run-rate credit cost impact 4–5bps.** FCNR-B/ECB/OFCB programme of USD 2.3–2.5bn underway; USD 775mn raised in July. ECLGS 5.0: INR10,000cr+ disbursed of an INR18,000cr pool. New MD & CEO Brajesh Kumar Singh has reset priorities to efficiency over growth.
- _Q2 FY27 → check: did the SMA-2/SMA-0 spike reverse as the government-guaranteed accounts normalised; NIM trajectory toward 2.60% as bulk deposits are replaced by FCNR-B; did July FCNR-B cross USD 1bn and is the USD 2.3–2.5bn annual programme on track; CASA moving toward 30–32%; ECL dry run completed in October; residual ECLGS 5.0 disbursement of INR5,000–6,000cr; branch openings against the 250 target; whether profit growth recovers once the PSLC seasonal spike rolls off and treasury stabilises._
